Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Colgate-Palmolive, Kimberly-Clark, BJ's Wholesale and Ollie's Bargain Outlet
sum: Chicago, IL – November 13, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Colgate-Palmolive Co. CL, Kimberly-Clark Corp. KMB, BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. BJ and Ollie's Bargain Outlet Holdings, Inc. OLLI.
Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3028520/4-consumer-staples-stocks-to-watch-amid-industry-headwinds

The Consumer Products-Staples industry is navigating a challenging operating environment as persistent cost pressures, elevated living expenses and heightened consumer price sensitivity influence purchasing decisions. Consumers are increasingly seeking value, switching pack sizes, looking for promotions and trading down within categories, creating demand volatility. Meanwhile, elevated raw material, labor and transportation costs, alongside operating expenses, continue to pressure margins. Currency fluctuations and trade-related uncertainty further complicate the industry's operating landscape.

Amid these challenges, consumer staples companies are focusing on productivity, cost optimization and supply-chain efficiency while investing in product innovation, digital capabilities and portfolio optimization to support long-term growth. Efforts to strengthen brand positioning, expand distribution and enhance consumer engagement remain important. Colgate-Palmolive Co., Kimberly-Clark Corp., BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. and Ollie's Bargain Outlet Holdings, Inc. are leveraging operational efficiencies, value-focused offerings and strategic initiatives to navigate industry headwinds and strengthen their competitive positions.

The Zacks Consumer Products-Staples industry includes companies that manufacture, market and distribute a broad range of everyday household and personal-use items. These offerings span personal care products, cleaning tools, stationery, bed and bath essentials and general household goods such as small appliances, cutlery and food-storage solutions.

Some players also participate in categories like batteries, lighting, pet food, treats and related supplies. Their products reach consumers through supermarkets, drug and grocery chains, department stores, mass merchandisers, warehouse clubs and other retail partners, while a growing share is now sold through digital channels.

items.t: Colgate-Palmolive India stock set for INR 24 interim dividend
sum: Colgate-Palmolive India reported stronger quarterly sales and profit on October 22, 2026, according to Moneycontrol. The report covered the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Net profit rose 4.2 percent year over year to INR 342 crore from INR 328 crore. Revenue from operations increased 12.2 percent to INR 1,705.7 crore, while net sales reached about INR 1,692 crore compared with INR 1,507 crore a year earlier.

The toothpaste portfolio delivered high-single-digit volume growth, supported by the premium range and Colgate MaxFresh. Moneycontrol reported that the company increased spending on brand building and premiumisation during the quarter.

EBITDA increased 1.9 percent year over year to INR 474 crore from INR 465 crore. The EBITDA margin nevertheless declined to 28 percent from 31 percent, showing that operating costs and investment spending grew faster than earnings.

Gross margin expanded by 40 basis points to 69.6 percent. Management said it plans to address commodity-cost volatility through cost savings and calibrated pricing while continuing to invest in products and advertising.
The board approved an interim dividend of INR 24 per share for fiscal 2026-27. Shareholders recorded on November 2, 2026, are eligible, and payment is scheduled to begin on November 19, 2026.

Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE:CL) Consumer Defensive Colgate-Palmolive Company (NYSE:CL) 98.49 USD +0.485 0.495% Last Updated at: 2026-11-12T15:46:00Z raised its full-year earnings guidance after reporting quarterly results that showed broader sales growth, a wider gross margin and Base Business earnings per share ahead of Wall Street expectations, according to the company's release filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission late last month. The update keeps Colgate-Palmolive firmly on the radar of investors tracking Consumer Stocks.

The oral care, personal care, home care and pet nutrition group said net sales rose by a mid-single-digit percentage to several billion dollars, while organic sales, which strip out currency moves and portfolio changes, increased modestly. Shares of Colgate-Palmolive trade on the New York Stock Exchange, which places the stock in the NYSE Composite, and it is also a constituent of the S&P 500 and the Russell 1000. Base Business earnings per share rose by a high-single-digit percentage, and the company now expects full-year Base Business earnings growth at a solid rate, up from its earlier mid-single-digit guidance.

According to the company's earnings tables filed on Form 8-K, net sales rose modestly from the prior-year quarter. Modest organic sales growth included a small drag from the decision to exit private label pet food, a business Colgate has been winding down.

Gross margin widened meaningfully on both a reported basis and a Base Business basis, according to the company's tables. For a consumer products group of Colgate's size, gains of that magnitude are meaningful, because they fund higher advertising while still lifting operating earnings.

The raised 2026 guidance and third quarter update come on top of strong recent momentum, with Colgate-Palmolive's share price up 11.12% over the past month and delivering a 26.26% year-to-date share price return, while the 5-year total shareholder return of 41.85% points to a steadier long-term payoff as investors respond to both earnings delivery and evolving expectations for future growth and risk.

According to rcb9, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who built the narrative model, the key step is stripping out the skin health impairment to understand what the underlying toothpaste and pet food franchise is truly earning.

Start by correcting the margin. Screens show Colgate earning about 10% net. Cash was never touched: operating cash flow set a record at $4.198 billion.

items.t: Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE:CL) Q3 2026: Guidance Raised
sum: Consumer staples leaders are often judged on consistency, and Colgate-Palmolive Company (NYSE:CL) Consumer Defensive Colgate-Palmolive Company (NYSE:CL) 98.63 USD +0.690 0.705% Last Updated at: 2026-11-10T17:52:00Z delivered just that in its third-quarter 2026 report on October 30. The New York-based maker of toothpaste, soap, household cleaners and pet food grew net sales and organic sales, with growth across all four of its categories and four of its five divisions. It also raised its full-year gross profit margin and base business earnings per share guidance. For readers who follow Consumer Stocks, Colgate shows how a global brand portfolio can sustain growth in a challenging consumer environment.

Net sales increased, and organic sales, which exclude currency effects and acquisitions, also grew. A small negative impact came from lower private label pet food sales. The chairman, president and chief executive described the quarter as another strong one, with broad-based top- and bottom-line growth.
Growth spanned oral care, personal care, home care and pet nutrition. Four of the company's five divisions grew both net and organic sales, demonstrating geographic breadth.

Colgate's global market share in toothpaste remained at a leading level year to date, and it maintained leadership in manual toothbrushes. These positions reflect decades of brand building and broad distribution in both developed and emerging markets.

Colgate narrowed its full-year net sales growth guidance and now expects organic sales growth broadly in line with its nine-month performance. It raised its guidance for gross profit margin and for base business earnings per share. Higher gross margin guidance indicates pricing, productivity and mix are offsetting cost pressures effectively.

Oral care is Colgate's largest and most important category. Toothpaste, toothbrushes and mouthwash are sold in more than two hundred countries and territories. Premium innovations, such as whitening and sensitivity products, support pricing.
Personal care includes brands such as Palmolive, Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick. These products serve everyday hygiene needs.

Colgate-Palmolive vs. Kraft Heinz: With the Market Turmoil, Which Stock Is a Better Buy?
sum: With the recent market turmoil, investors may start looking more closely at defensive stocks like Colgate-Palmolive (CL -2.16%) and Kraft Heinz (KHC -2.80%).

Colgate-Palmolive dominates personal care categories like toothpaste, while Kraft Heinz focuses on massive scale within the packaged food industry. This comparison breaks down their latest performance and valuation to help you decide which belongs in your portfolio.

Colgate-Palmolive operates a diverse business model focused on oral care, personal care, home care, and pet nutrition. The company sells its products in more than 200 countries, reaching a vast global audience of consumers, dentists, and veterinarians. In its latest annual report, the company noted that Walmart (WMT -1.72%) and its affiliates accounted for approximately 11% of sales. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $20.4 billion, which represented growth of approximately 1.4% compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of roughly $2.1 billion for the period. This resulted in a net margin of nearly 10.5%, indicating a decrease from the approximately 14.4% net margin recorded during the previous fiscal year.

Kraft Heinz is a global food and beverage giant producing items for at-home, restaurant, and on-the-go occasions. As a major player among food stocks, the company operates in multiple countries and relies on a mix of independent brokers and direct sales. In its latest annual report, the company noted that Walmart represented approximately 21% of net sales in FY 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $24.9 billion, a decrease of approximately 3.5% from the previous year. The company reported a net loss of nearly $5.8 billion for the fiscal period. This led to a net margin of roughly -23.4%, which was a significant shift from the positive net margin reported in the prior fiscal year.

Colgate-Palmolive faces risks from its extensive international operations, where foreign currency fluctuations and geopolitical instability can impact financial results. The company competes in an intense global market against private labels and direct-to-consumer brands that challenge its pricing power.

sum: Fresh earnings are driving the conversation around Colgate-Palmolive (CL) after the consumer products group reported third quarter 2026 results and lifted its full year outlook for sales and profitability.

Colgate-Palmolive's recent Q3 beat and higher full year guidance come after a strong run, with the share price delivering a 24.29% year to date return and a 25.54% total shareholder return over the past year, even though the stock slipped 2.16% on the day after the results.

After Colgate-Palmolive's strong run and modest pullback, the share price now sits between its recent high, analyst targets and intrinsic estimates. Where does fair value really land within that range?

Colgate-Palmolive closed at $96.56, while the most followed narrative, according to rcb9, points to a fair value of $86.48 using a 7% discount rate. That gap frames the latest Q3 beat as impressive on execution but tight on valuation headroom.

A note on the shape of this result. Twenty four times forward Base Business earnings of roughly $3.88 implies about $93 today. This model returns $86.48. The whole difference is structural. When the discount rate exceeds the growth rate, five years at a three point gap costs about 16%. For a slow compounder this method is inherently more conservative than a simple multiple, and that is worth knowing before treating the output as a verdict rather than as one lens.
Still, this fair value lens could crack if North America stays weak for longer or if another impairment in skin health hits Colgate-Palmolive earnings quality.

Is Procter & Gamble Stock Priced Right Against Its Peers?
sum: Procter & Gamble (PG) operates with a wider operating margin than its four rivals in household and personal care: Colgate-Palmolive, Church & Dwight, Estee Lauder and Kenvue. Over the past year, however, P&G stock returned the least of the five. Investors currently pay less for its earnings than they do for Church & Dwight’s. So how much less are you paying, and for how much more profit?

P&G stock currently trades at 22.2 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 31.8 times for Church & Dwight. Profitability metrics highlight a different balance. P&G had an operating margin of 22.7% over the same period, well above the 17.5% recorded for Church & Dwight. The two companies belong to different industry classifications, so what each sells may account for part of that margin gap. P&G also delivered faster top-line expansion, with revenue up 3.3% against 2.7% for Church & Dwight.

Colgate-Palmolive and Estee Lauder each recorded a loss in at least one of the past four quarters, so their P/Es do not provide a direct comparison with P&G’s. Among the peers, only Kenvue carries a lower P/E at 20.6 times earnings, and that company saw its revenue grow more slowly at 1.8%.
P&G is keeping a smaller portion of its sales as profit. The company posted an operating margin of 24% a year earlier, compared with 22.7% over the past twelve months.

In the latest quarter, revenue grew 1.5% from a year earlier. Management noted that market growth across North America and its main European markets has slowed by 1 to 2 points over the past 12 to 18 months.

Management is currently betting on better products to restart growth. Tide Original Liquid went from declining sales to high-single-digit growth after P&G improved the detergent without raising the price. Tide Evo, a new formula that P&G has patented, is set to roll out nationally in fiscal 2027.

Management expects organic sales to grow 1% to 3% in fiscal 2027, matching the expansion range it anticipates for its markets. Executives forecast core earnings per share of $6.89 to $7.11, compared with $6.89 in fiscal 2026. Hitting the low end of that guidance means no growth at all.

Campbell's, The Marzetti Company, and Colgate-Palmolive Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
sum: A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after investors rotated out of semiconductors and AI names during the global chip selloff.

The S&P 500 consumer staples sector gained about 1.7%, the best of all 11 sectors, while the S&P 500 fell more than 1%. Packaged-food names led: Conagra Brands rose about 5% and General Mills more than 3%, with Procter & Gamble up near 2%.This was likely a defensive rotation as the chip/AI selloff and hawkish rate repricing pressuring semiconductors pushed capital into stable-cash-flow defensives.

When investors question stretched AI valuations and brace for tighter policy under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, the reflex is to hide in sectors whose demand doesn't track the economic cycle.Staples are often considered cheaper and pay dividends, the natural landing spot for money leaving high-multiple chips.

The leadership pattern confirms it: low-multiple, high-yield packaged-food names (Conagra, General Mills) led the rebound, while pricier or more discretionary staples (Estée Lauder) and a beverage laggard (Dr Pepper) were left behind.A one-day rotation triggered by a chip selloff is fragile. If AI names stabilize, Wedbush already framed the selloff as a buying opportunity, these flows can reverse fast, and staples are themselves rate-sensitive bond proxies exposed to the same hawkish repricing that started the move.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Interview: Diana Schildhouse, chief data and analytics officer, Colgate-Palmolive
sum: Diana Schildhouse, chief data and analytics officer at Colgate-Palmolive, describes herself as a data storyteller – but what does that mean in terms of day-to-day delivery?
“To be successful in roles like this, you must have a deep connection with the business and understand what you’re trying to solve, what their questions are, and then devise solutions,” she says.
“Those solutions could use advanced analytics. Sometimes, it’s about creating simpler solutions. But success is always about solving that business need.”

Schildhouse joined Colgate-Palmolive in April 2021 as chief analytics and insights officer. She was previously at Mattel for eight years, latterly as senior vice-president for global strategy, insights and analytics. Schildhouse has also worked for Westfield, Merrill Lynch and Disney.
“Most of my experience has been in consumer-facing companies,” she says.

“In terms of my career, I’ve always been in functions like advanced analytics, insights and strategy. When I saw the opportunity with Colgate-Palmolive, I thought about the breadth and scale of the company. It was an exciting opportunity for me to come in and build from the ground up, while leveraging the scale of the business.”

Schildhouse joined the company in a newly created role to develop an analytics and insights strategy for an organisation that operates in over 200 countries and territories globally. After proving her success in this role, she assumed her current position in June 2025, where the breadth of responsibilities increased to include oversight for data and artificial intelligence (AI).
